english: Ten lines are drawn in a plane so that no two of them are parallel and no three of them pass through a common point. Let $B$ and $U$ be the numbers of bounded and unbounded regions, respectively, into which these lines divide the plane. Then the value of $\dfrac{B}{U}$ is ______.
hindi: एक तल में दस रेखाएँ इस प्रकार खींची जाती हैं कि उनमें से कोई दो समान्तर नहीं हैं और कोई तीन एक उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दु से नहीं गुजरतीं। माना कि ये रेखाएँ तल को जितने परिबद्ध तथा अपरिबद्ध क्षेत्रों में विभाजित करती हैं, उनकी संख्याएँ क्रमशः $B$ तथा $U$ हैं। तब $\dfrac{B}{U}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The $k$-th line meets the previous $k-1$ lines in $k-1$ new points, is cut into $k$ pieces and adds $k$ regions
Unbounded: a large circle enclosing all $\binom{10}{2}=45$ intersection points meets the lines in 20 points, giving 20 arcs, one per unbounded region: $U=20$
solution_full: Add the lines one at a time. The $k$-th line meets the previous $k-1$ lines in $k-1$ distinct points (no two parallel, no three concurrent), so it is divided into $k$ pieces, and each piece splits one existing region into two: the $k$-th line adds $k$ regions.
Starting from 1 region: $R=1+(1+2+\cdots+10)=1+55=56$. Equivalently $R=1+n+\binom{n}{2}$ with $\binom{10}{2}=45$ points of intersection.

Draw a circle large enough to contain all 45 points of intersection. Each line crosses it twice, giving 20 points on the circle and 20 arcs. Outside the circle no two lines meet, so each unbounded region contains exactly one arc, and each arc lies in one unbounded region: $U=20$.
originality_note: New: the split of the regions formed by lines in general position into bounded and unbounded ones, using the line-by-line region count and a large circle for the unbounded regions (way 5). Closest known: 'n lines in general position divide the plane into 1 + n + C(n,2) regions'. Different because: the unbounded regions must be counted separately (2n), which is not the usual exercise.
blueprint_concepts: Number of points of intersection and regions formed by lines

concept_use.Number of points of intersection and reg: The number of regions 1 + n + C(n,2) comes from the C(10,2) = 45 points of intersection; the unbounded ones are counted by the 2n arcs of a large circle.
